title: Role of corticostriatal connectivity in chronic back pain and its possible affectation by an interdisciplinary multimodal pain therapy
summary:
Chronic back pain causes high costs for the health system and has often far-reaching negative effects on those who are affected. To prevent chronification, an early prediction of the tendency of subacute pain to become chronic is important. One of the best predictions was made by a group from the USA in 2012 using functional connectivity in the brain measured with fMRI. 
The primary aim of the study is to compare the functional connectivity in the brain in patients with chronic back pain (PwCBP) with gender- and age-matched control persons. This allows to assess the prognostic value of this parameter.  
A second goal is to investigate whether this parameter can be changed by an interdisciplinary multimodal pain therapy (IMPT). IMPT has been shown to significantly improve clinical symptoms, especially pain intensity and functional impairment in PwCBP. We hypothesize that IMPT can also normalize the functional connectivity in the brain.
In order to examine our questions, PwCBP, who were assigned to the Pain Clinic of the University Hospital Jena for IMPT, will be asked to voluntarily participate in two MRI / fMRI examinations. Our questions can be answered from the comparisons of data before and after IMPT.
conditions: Chronic pain syndrom (with somatic and psychological factors)

interventions.name: Chronic back pain patients that are administered as their standard therapy to an Interdisciplinary multimodal pain therapy (IMPT) at the Day hospital for pain of the University Hospital Jena (UKJ)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Screening for IMPT completed, accepted for IMPT, chronic back pain as primary aim for referral to IMPT
Exclusion criteria:
Previous traumatic brain injury (influence on FK_NAc-mPFC)
Exclusion from MRI (separate exclusion criteria like ferromagnetic parts in the body, old black tattoos, claustrophobia)
